title: Cocktail 2 Just Invented the Bollywood Music Festival. Three Cities. One Film. Pure Mayhem.
excerpt: Shahid Kapoor, Kriti Sanon and Rashmika Mandanna will party live with fans across Mumbai, Delhi and Pune — with original singers performing every track — before the film even opens on June 19.
body:
Forget the standard press junket. Forget the polite appearance at a mall in Bandra where someone shoves a mic in **Shahid Kapoor**'s face and asks him what his favourite song from the album is. **Cocktail 2** is doing something that Bollywood has genuinely never done before — a full-scale, multi-city music festival, hitting Mumbai, New Delhi and Pune, where the film's original singers will perform the entire soundtrack live on stage, the star cast will show up to party alongside thousands of fans, and the whole thing is being treated less like a promotional event and more like a cultural happening.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=XXxUqLHq1xg</youtube>

And honestly? It's about time.

**Maddock Films** and **Luv Films** — the powerhouse producing duo behind the sequel — have been watching the numbers, and the numbers are obscene. "Mashooqa," the Shahid-Kriti romantic banger shot across the sunlit cliffs of Sicily, hasn't just charted — it has camped out at the top of Spotify and YouTube like it's paying rent. The track has become the kind of earworm that soundtracks every Instagram reel, every pre-wedding sangeet playlist, and every late-night Uber ride home. If you haven't heard it yet, check your pulse.

And now they've dropped "Vallah," the latest single from the album, adding more fuel to a soundtrack that already had the industry talking. Composed by **Pritam Chakraborty** — who previewed two tracks at an exclusive Mumbai media event last month and reportedly left the room silent — the Cocktail 2 soundtrack is shaping up to be the most commercially dominant film album of 2026. "Tujhko," the **Arijit Singh**-sung emotional gut-punch centred on Shahid and **Rashmika Mandanna**'s characters, was the other early reveal. Sources at that preview described grown journalists going quiet. That's the Arijit effect.

The festival itself is designed to feel like a concert first, promotion second. Think live performances under stadium lights, behind-the-scenes revelations, audience singalongs, maybe a few tears if Arijit shows up and drops "Tujhko" live. Shahid, **Kriti Sanon** and Rashmika will all be present — not sitting on a stage behind a table, but actually inside the experience, sharing set stories, engaging with fans, and becoming part of the performances.

> "This isn't just a music launch — it's a live cinematic universe experience." — Maddock Films

Directed by **Homi Adajania**, who gave us the original *Cocktail* back in 2012 — the film that quietly made Deepika Padukone a superstar and turned "Tumhi Ho Bandhu" into a generational anthem — the sequel carries the brand name but brings an entirely new cast and emotional dynamic. Shahid plays the romantic lead opposite both Kriti and Rashmika, in what producers **Dinesh Vijan** and **Luv Ranjan** are calling a stylish romantic entertainer about love, heartbreak, friendship and the beautiful mess in between.

For the diaspora, this is the film you'll be planning a group outing for. Cocktail 2 releases worldwide on **June 19**, and if the music festival energy translates even partially to the cinema experience, multiplexes are going to feel like nightclubs. The original *Cocktail* was a film that NRIs adopted as their own — Diana Penty in that white dress, Deepika's transformation, Saif's irresponsible charm — and the sequel is clearly angling for the same emotional territory.

The strategy is also a signal to the industry. In a June packed with nine major releases and ₹1,400 crore at stake, standing out requires more than a good trailer. Cocktail 2 is betting that if you make the promotion itself the event — if you give people a reason to *feel* something before they buy a ticket — the box office takes care of itself.

With the trailer trending, "Mashooqa" refusing to leave anyone's playlist, "Vallah" adding yet another anthem to the collection, and now a live festival tour sweeping across three cities, this isn't just a movie launch. It's a mood. And Bollywood hasn't felt this kind of pre-release electricity since the *Pathaan* mania of 2023.

June 19 can't come fast enough.
